results.sources_checked: Channel A five-source battery run 2026-08-29 (search window 2025-08-12 -> 2026-08-29). (1) Company newsroom/blog: openai.com blocks direct requests (403) so pages were read through the Wayback Machine. Wayback CDX enumeration of openai.com/index/* for mental-health/well-being slugs plus targeted slug probes returned the following post-finding pages, all read in full and none mentioning Weval or the Collective Intelligence Project: "Strengthening ChatGPT's responses in sensitive conversations" (2025-10-27), "Expert Council on Well-Being and AI" (2025-10-14), "Our approach to mental health-related litigation" (2025-11-25), "Funding grants for new research into AI and mental health" (2025-12-01, updated 2026-01-28), "An update on our mental health-related work" (2026-02-27); also read "Helping people when they need it most" (2025-08-26), "Teen safety, freedom and privacy" (2025-09-16) and the GPT-5.1 launch page - no mention of the evaluator. (2) Next model/system card(s) for the family: The GPT-4o system card itself (2024-08-08) predates the finding. The next general-purpose card for the ChatGPT model family after 2025-08-12 is the GPT-5 system card dated 2025-08-13 (cdn.openai.com/gpt-5-system-card.pdf, read in full, 131k chars): it discusses self-harm/safe-completions but contains no occurrence of "Weval" or "Collective Intelligence". Post-finding cards located via Wayback CDX and availability API: GPT-5.1-Codex-Max system card (2025-11-19, read in full, no Weval/CIP mention, no mental-health section); gpt-5-2-codex-system-card and gpt-5-3-codex-system-card exist (snapshots 2026-08-26) but both openai.com and the Wayback copies failed to decode on 2026-08-29 (ContentDecodingError / connection refused) - recorded as unread, not as absence; no gpt-5-1/5-2/5-3 non-Codex system-card slug exists in the Wayback index. (3) Safety/deployment hubs and changelogs: openai.com/safety, OpenAI Safety Evaluations Hub (openai.com/safety/evaluations-hub) and the Model Spec 2025-10-27 revision - none mentions Weval or the Collective Intelligence Project. (4) Company response inside the evaluator's own report: the weval.org aggregate model card is auto-generated and contains no OpenAI statement - the string "OpenAI" does not occur anywhere on the page (re-verified 2026-08-29). (5) Open web search to locate company primary sources: WebSearch quota exhausted this session; used Google News RSS, Hacker News Algolia, OpenAlex, Marginalia and DuckDuckGo/Bing/Brave/Mojeek/SearXNG (the last five blocked by CAPTCHA or 403) - no OpenAI primary document about Weval was located. NEGATIVE-LAG INVALIDATIONS: GPT-4o system card, 2024-08-08 (cdn.openai.com/gpt-4o-system-card.pdf) predates the finding and is not a coordinated pre-deployment disclosure -> invalid. GPT-5 system card, dated 2025-08-13 on its face (cdn.openai.com/gpt-5-system-card.pdf, released 2025-08-07) - although dated one day after the finding it contains no reference to Weval or the Collective Intelligence Project and no attributable change, so it is not a response. EXCLUDED AS NON-ATTRIBUTABLE STANDING/PARALLEL WORK: OpenAI's 2025-10-27 sensitive-conversations update and the associated Model Spec revision are substantive changes in the same domain, but they credit only OpenAI's own clinician network and Expert Council, name no external evaluator, and state that they "build on our existing principles"; no causal link to the Weval card exists, so under section 8 they are not a response to this finding. Not found: any OpenAI primary document responding to, citing or acknowledging the Weval / Collective Intelligence Project GPT-4o model card (checked 2026-08-29). Channel B log: Channel B battery run 2026-08-29, search terms "Weval", "weval.org", "Collective Intelligence Project". US: Federal Register API (conditions[term]=Weval and ="Collective Intelligence Project") -> 0 documents; govinfo full-text search API (www.govinfo.gov/wssearch/search) -> "Weval" 3 hits, all pre-1990 OCR false positives (CZIC-hc107-c23-e44-1983 Aliso Greenbelt plan; SERIALSET-11451 Foreign commerce 1946; SERIALSET-07496 Navy register), "weval.org" 0 hits, "Collective Intelligence Project" + "Weval" 0 hits; congress.gov search pages 403 so govinfo (CREC/CDOC/CRPT collections) was used as the substitute. UK: Hansard search API (Commons + Lords) -> "Weval" TotalContributions 0; "Collective Intelligence Project" 74 hits, all unrelated word-level matches (e.g. Lords 2025-05-09, Commons 2025-01-23) with no reference to the evaluator; gov.uk search API -> "Weval" total 0 (covers ministerial statements, DSIT/AISI, ICO and NCSC pages published on gov.uk). committees.parliament.uk search returned 403 and could not be read. EU: EUR-Lex quick search and European Parliament document register are JS-rendered and returned no readable result set. Not found: any official government source citing Weval, weval.org or this Collective Intelligence Project model card (checked 2026-08-29).
results.media_outlets: Not found: independent press coverage of this Weval model card (Google News RSS, checked 2026-08-29: query "weval" returns 46 items, all about the Dutch electronic duo Weval - Radio Milwaukee 2026-04-03, PopMatters 2025-10-07, Silent Radio 2025-09-16, Resident Advisor 2026-08-05 etc.; query "Weval GPT-5 mental health" returns 0 items). Only news item referencing the platform: Tech Policy Press, "Women, Peace and Security Frameworks Must Apply to Defense AI", 2026-04-21 (https://www.techpolicy.press/women-peace-and-security-frameworks-must-apply-to-defense-ai/), which cites weval.org for an unrelated Women-Peace-and-Security benchmark, not for this mental-health finding.
results.academic_citations: Morrin H, Au Yeung J, Agnew Z, Ostergaard SD, Pollak T, "It Is the Journey, Not the Destination: Moving From End Points to Trajectories When Assessing Chatbot Mental Health Safety", JMIR Mental Health, 2026-03-04, doi:10.2196/91454 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13052998/) - cites Weval mental-health blueprint runs as refs 22 and 23 (https://weval.org/analysis/mh_z_tests__mh1 and the Stanford HAI mental health safety eval run) [CAVEAT: co-author Zarinah Agnew is declared "clinical lead at the Collective Intelligence Project", i.e. the evaluator, so this is only partly independent; and it cites Weval analysis pages, not the aggregate model card]. Bao H, Huang Y, Wang X, Zhang Z, Zhou Y, Yang C, Zhang X, Ye Y, "Position: General Alignment Has Hit a Ceiling; Edge Alignment Must Be Taken Seriously", arXiv:2602.20042, submitted 2026-02-23 - cites the Weval platform generically, not this model card. OpenAlex full-text search (checked 2026-08-29): "weval.org" -> count 1 (the JMIR paper above); "Weval" + "Collective Intelligence Project" -> count 1 (the arXiv paper above). Not found: any academic citation of the weval.org aggregate model card for this model (OpenAlex + Semantic Scholar Graph API title/abstract search, 2026-08-29).
results.social_highlights: Hacker News (Algolia API, checked 2026-08-29): query "weval.org" -> 24 hits; the only submission of the platform itself is "A Platform to Build and Share AI Evaluations", https://weval.org/, 2026-01-19, 1 point (item 46677413); remaining hits are passing comment mentions (e.g. "Launch HN: Parachute (YC S25) - Guardrails for Clinical AI", 2025-08-20, item 44958908). Query "weval" -> top hits are the unrelated Cranelift/WASM "weval" partial evaluator. Not found: any public discussion thread about the GPT-4o or GPT-5 Weval aggregate model card.

results.notes: Finding re-verified against https://weval.org/cards/gpt-4o on 2026-08-29: the page carries the exact sentence "Deploying this model in high-stakes mental health crisis intervention without stringent, explicit system prompts could lead to severe safety failures, including providing harmful information or colluding with dangerous ideations, as demonstrated in Stanford HAI Mental Health Safety: LLM Appropriateness in Crisis Scenarios." and the Behavioral Patterns line "Without such prompts, its behavior can become inconsistent or even problematic". Evaluator = Weval (Collective Intelligence Project); company = OpenAI. Access constraints logged: openai.com serves 403 to both fetch.py and WebFetch, so every OpenAI page was read via the Wayback Machine; two 2026 Codex system cards could not be decoded and are recorded as unread rather than as absence; this session's WebSearch quota was exhausted before any Channel A query, so open-web search was done with Google News RSS, HN Algolia, OpenAlex, govinfo, Hansard and gov.uk APIs.
